approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a score-ranked population of molecular graphs using quantile-based parent draws, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary graph mutations. It creates fresh surplus pools, rejects unstable or duplicate identities, and admits a novel candidate only when its sulfur signatures do not exceed the largest corresponding count in its original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process learns from the complete chronological archive of accepted task-local scores using folded integer Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product count-Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores by the archive mean and population standard deviation, then uses correlated posterior function draws with stable masked choices to allocate each announced batch. Greedy survival and real accepted feedback drive later breeding; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange remains disabled.
approach.novelty: I replace the covariance by the fixed square of the Parent's count-Tanimoto similarity. This one zero-preserving integer-power sharpening weakens partial similarity while retaining count magnitude information, unit self-similarity and exact fingerprint aliases. It may improve ranking and productive exploration, but may also fragment useful extrapolation. No completed same-Parent sibling is supplied. The concurrent exponential mean and residual-path experiments examine a different law at separate output boundaries; this experiment coherently changes the complete train, cross and pool covariance. Earlier min/max overlap, normalized Matérn, unfolded counts, added atom-pair information and exponential covariance failures remain specific counterexamples, not evidence that squaring will work.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-1744a1494180 still has limited productive exploration: its complete 4,350 accepted offspring contain 648 strict best-generating-parent beats and 255 sequential incumbent improvements, with only 2,469 nonterminal offspring later reused. Its matched mean endpoint is 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878; the sulfur-gate transfer changed its own Parent mean by +0.0007834645552323346, below the gain target, with seed deltas +0.017686193676039963,+0.002307179813052951,-0.01764297982339591. The limiting behavior is accepted allocation that often fails to deliver productive absolute progress. Weak partial count-Tanimoto covariance is a candidate explanation, not an identified mediator. On the older exchange-free baseline n-62daf219c70a, exponential covariance n-07dd356cb779 improved same-selected-stream prediction/ranking yet lost 0.032277693549492024 in mean endpoint; normalized Matérn n-ea03f38e7e10 lost 0.02750824038854201 and ranked its own accepted stream worse than the passive original. Count removal n-e00db808bbb4 lost 0.051295849138213355, unfolding n-b14daceabbeb lost 0.04816296717262832 and the equal atom-pair mixture n-e75f0f495f9b lost 0.033408159038087325. Exact min/max n-dd2b25d32925 lost 0.04824526182151967. All are retained under their original Parent and conditions; none measures the current sulfur-gated squared law, establishes floor mediation or supports a familywide conclusion.
hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count-Tanimoto covariance T_DP by the fixed squared law K(x,y)=T_DP(x,y)**2 on unchanged folded Morgan integer occurrence rows, coherently in every GP Gram block while preserving inherited zero/unit conventions and exact T_DP=1 aliases.

finding_summary.headline: Squared covariance changes real exploration but loses endpoint score despite modest ranking and core-reuse gains
finding_summary.insights: This exposed test separates genuine allocation and discovery-to-reuse delivery from useful final optimization. Weakening partial covariance while preserving zeros and count magnitude can produce more productive new cores and modestly better selected-stream ordering, yet still reduce absolute incumbent progress and endpoints. The exact fixed exponent-two route has exhausted its registered test; more novelty, narrower dispersion and ranking gains do not rescue it. Exact count aliases remain, so the route does not resolve representation collisions. The chemistry report finds recognizable amides and aryl cyclic amines alongside reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds, cyanate/acyl-fluoride or cumulated unsaturation, unresolved ring geometry and unspecified states; stronger Parent structures also have liabilities. Neither core novelty nor those differences identify chemical mediation. Passive alternatives have no labels or continued ancestry, and shared descendants do not prove independent scaffold contribution. Current composition review, whole-foundation and constituent coverage, full-current-condition and joint interactions, chemical mediation, full-history processing and partial lineage composition remain open. The distinct concurrent exponential output-path probes and historical kernel failures cannot be pooled into a covariance-floor, mean/residual or universal kernel conclusion.
finding_summary.results: The squared covariance ran throughout all three seeds and five tasks, changed 1,442 accepted choices relative to original preferences on the same masks, and added 1,209 accepted records outside the passive original sets. On those actual accepted labels, pair accuracy rose from 0.73967 to 0.74039 and mean batch Spearman from 0.59327 to 0.59635, but MSE worsened from 0.0092124 to 0.0094384. Productive new typed/generic cores increased from 262/163 to 287/197, and later-used sources with useful accepted descendants from 146/91 to 176/121. This did not produce stronger overall progress: sequential incumbent gains fell from 255 to 242 and their summed magnitude from 5.81942 to 5.15234. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.551982, a paired loss of 0.044472 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros fell; fourteen of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell. Macro dispersion narrowed from 0.033970 to 0.016362.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive bonds and unresolved geometry, alongside recognizable amides and cyclic amines
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-36a7bb9883ec generates compact fused azaaryl carbonyl/thione systems, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated dione/imino systems. Rings and aromatic regions are abundant: digest ring-closure incidence ranges from 0.9494 to 0.9782 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9299 to 0.9724. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions; some unusual aromatic SMILES labels do not survive RDKit aromatic-ring perception. All charged and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0, although potentially basic aliphatic nitrogen and unassigned tetrahedral centres are present. Global diversity is moderate, with distinct seed families but repeated close substitutions within leaders. Recognizable medicinal fragments coexist with direct N-halogen bonds, O-halogen attachments, cumulated unsaturation, N/O/S linkages and dense or small connected rings. Parsing is not evidence of synthetic access, geometry, stability or pharmacology. The inherited sulfur condition cannot certify those properties, and this assessment does not reconstruct gate decisions or certify absolute envelope compliance.

All 15 Child and 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent trajectories were present and read, spanning five tasks and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. Each side has 900 records per task, including 870 optimizer records; every Child digest counter, count and excerpt molecule/score/evaluation join matches. No task, path or paired seed is absent. context.comparison states child_complete=true and paired_complete=true without profile mismatch. The comparison uses the published current Parent, not older n-62daf219c70a endpoints. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not final Top-1 molecules; all seed endpoints below come from the full chronology. Child cited_smiles are supported by its digest or the request's trusted Child trajectory list; Parent structures are described from published comparison paths, which are not additional citation authority. CPU-only offline RDKit descriptors and path hashes are recorded in .slots/round-0027-slot-2/molecular_evidence_audit.json.

The Parent's full original molecular assessment was read through context.evidence_index. Recurring local-bond, geometry, unspecified-state, context-preservation and plausible-alternative gaps originated in n-c55c3d520a2c, continued through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and remain conditional output associations in this Child at 300 observations per task on the issued Search panel. The exact declared neutral sulfur envelope from n-93cd9a000278 remains a source condition; older numerical effects are not pooled or transferred. These molecules neither identify the component causing a liability nor establish chemical mediation of a score difference. The pinned current composition remains needs_review pending scheduled catalog_review at round27 close under v-17b4d64669a7955c8e61ca7e. This chemistry report closes none of the whole-foundation m-4fa9546e559e, constituent, full-current-condition, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, full-history-processing or partial L07 composition gaps.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact 24-25-heavy-atom fused indole/azaindole-like systems linked to pyridyl regions by amide, thioamide or ketone connections. Seed 0 has an additional carbon bridge/ring and an N-hydroxy thioamide; seed 1 has an ordinary pyridyl amide but direct ring N-F; seed 2 has an N-H indole, vinyl group and pyridyl ketone. Methoxy, short alkyl and aryl halogen substituents recur. The optimizer median size is 25 heavy atoms versus Parent 24. Familiar azaaryl carbonyl chemistry is present, but the bridged thioamide and N-halogen variants have uncertain routine synthetic access.
liabilities: Direct N-F/N-Br substitution on an indole-like nitrogen is distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogen substitution and keeps synthetic plausibility questionable.
The N-hydroxy thioamide and additional bridged ring require local stability and geometry assessment; sulfur membership alone cannot answer it.
missing_features: Plausible independent realizations of the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement remain limited among leaders; the Parent supplies a conventional halogen-free alternative that this Child's leaders do not reproduce.
Consistently conventional local bonding around ring nitrogen and the carbonyl/thione link is unresolved; the observed gradient supplies no exact missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145; Child seed endpoints are 0.4369542269692598, 0.4387992465191 and 0.4254027310763201. Small molecules such as methane and SBr score 0.0. Labels therefore associate with complete compact aromatic/carbonyl organization rather than isolated fragments. A tied leading series exchanges aryl F/Br/Cl and ring N-F/N-Br while retaining 0.4387992465191, so peripheral halogen identity is not uniquely established as the favorable feature. Parent reaches 0.4593573492521118 with a sulfur-free, halogen-free divinyl azaaryl N-hydroxy amide; its other endpoints are 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. The Child offers different thione/ketone arrangements without demonstrating a chemical reason for the paired label changes.

per_task.generated_character: This set contains the largest molecules, with a 36-heavy-atom optimizer median versus Parent 31. Child endpoints range from a 28-heavy-atom N-rich fused dione/thioimidate-like linked-ring system to a 46-heavy-atom linked heterocyclic framework bearing cumulated diene ether arms. Seed 1 instead has a 37-heavy-atom azaaryl/carbonyl/ether structure carrying O-C#N, a cyanate rather than an ordinary carbon-linked nitrile. Ring-closure and aromatic-string incidences are high, but the seed-0 leader has only one RDKit-perceived aromatic ring and the unusual seed-2 leader none: lowercase text is not proof of conventional aromatic stabilization. Dense small closures, unusual unsaturation and reactive peripheral groups make synthesis questionable.
liabilities: Cumulated double bonds are present at string incidence 0.0391, including the highest-label structure; extended ether-linked unsaturation raises local stability and synthesis questions.
Aromatic text labels span small fused closures and unusual ring bonding; no conformer or ring-strain evidence validates these graphs.
O-linked cyanate and azoalkene fragments require assessment separate from ordinary nitriles or amides.
missing_features: Geometrically credible, synthetically plausible alternatives preserving the successful heterocyclic relationship are not established among leading labels; the Parent's stronger example is itself chemically questionable.
Stable ordinary peripheral groups replacing cyanate, cumulene ether or azo functionality are not consistently represented in leaders. Their necessity is not established by these observations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Tiny fragments and the final azoalkene fragment CCC=C(Cl)N=NC sit at 0.5, while Child seed endpoints reach 0.6227999732316134, 0.615305470801107 and 0.6226258528489765. The initial linked aryl dione scores 0.548381482770623. The association favors particular connected heterocyclic arrangements over fragments, but tolerates cumulenes and dense ring topology. Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496: its strongest compact linked carbonyl/thione family also has O-F and halomethyl ether liabilities. The Child's larger seed-0 structure does not reach that label, so increased ring-rich mass and changed liabilities are not evidence of improved chemistry or objective fit.

per_task.generated_character: High labels accompany 26-29-heavy-atom aryl-substituted aliphatic amines with halogenated aromatic surfaces, phenol/methoxy/aniline groups and varied cyclic connections. Seed 0 uses a seven-membered unsaturated tertiary amine; seed 1 a five-membered diaza/aminal ring linked to an indane-like region and an aminoethyl aryl substituent; seed 2 a secondary amine adjacent to a substituted cyclopropane and bromomethyl group. Basic centres already exist despite entirely neutral notation. The optimizer median size is 32 heavy atoms versus Parent 29. These are comparatively recognizable medicinal arrangements, though the aminal, halomethyl group and unspecified stereochemical relationships require assessment.
liabilities: The five-membered diaza leader has an aminal environment whose stability should not be inferred from its label.
The seed-2 bromomethyl group is a different chemical liability from aryl bromine, and the successful cyclopropane-containing structure has unspecified stereochemistry.
Halogen-rich substitution and neutral-state notation do not establish solubility, exposure or pharmacological validity.
missing_features: Stereochemical identity and demonstrated conformations of the high-scoring cyclic/bridged arrangements remain absent, although their functional-group arrangement is recognizable.

A consistent set of conventional peripheral alternatives is not established around every successful amine family. Basic amine generation itself is already available and is not a supported missing capability.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-sulfonyl cyclic amine with N-chloro amide scores 0.00016650955053713697 and its cyclic ketone relative 0.00021169315013374197. Child endpoints rise to 0.9915381505306463, 0.9999881961692759 and 0.9489717884278961 in aryl/basic-amine arrangements. Parent endpoints are 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065, with different cyclic amine topologies. High labels associate with the overall aryl/aliphatic-amine organization, not presence of an extra N-halogen bond or sulfur: all three Child leaders are sulfur-free while the Parent's near-ceiling seven-membered diaza leader carries a methylthio substituent. No binding pose, protonation state or exact receptor pharmacophore follows from these scalar labels.

per_task.generated_character: This output joins fused quinoline/indole-like aromatic regions to larger nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems. Seed 2's 29-heavy-atom leader contains two N-methyl lactam-like carbonyls and a fused unsaturated N-containing ring linked through methylene to a methylquinoline. Seed 0 expands to a 36-heavy-atom alkoxyaryl/fused azaaryl/cyclic-urea-like arrangement with an N-isopropenyl substituent; seed 1 uses a 25-heavy-atom fused N-H aromatic system with a cyclic carbonyl and an N-C-N linkage. Optimizer median size is 30 heavy atoms versus Parent 31. Amide and azaaryl fragments are recognizable, but connected-ring geometry and local aminal/unsaturated environments keep makeability uncertain.
liabilities: Complex fused or medium nitrogen/carbonyl rings require geometry and route assessment beyond valence validity.
N-C-N/aminal and N-isopropenyl environments in alternate leaders merit separate local stability assessment; ordinary lactam carbonyls should not be conflated with those liabilities.
missing_features: Chemically independent, feasible alternatives retaining the favorable azaaryl/carbonyl relationship remain sparse among leaders; merely permuting similar ring connections supplies limited evidence of useful coverage.
Assigned stereochemical configurations and credible connected-ring conformations are not established where the cyclic frameworks require them.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Methane, oxygen and acetylene proposals score 0.0; the initial aryl nitrogen-rich dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Child seed endpoints are 0.21099810904413818, 0.20360741616532138 and 0.23133832961312736 versus Parent 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657. Higher labels retain azaaryl plus organized cyclic nitrogen/carbonyl regions. The strongest Child and Parent seed-2 structures both have 29 heavy atoms and the same molecular weight, but different connectivity: atom inventory alone does not account for the label. Late seed-2 proposals mostly retain this family at lower labels. No evidence identifies an exact absent target motif, and the narrow local ceiling does not prove complete scaffold collapse.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders have 26-29 heavy atoms and combine fluorinated, partly saturated N-containing rings with fused dione/carbonyl systems. Seed 0's leader has two direct N-F bonds, a fluorocyclohexenyl amino group and a partly unsaturated imine ring; seed 1 has a fluorophenol substituent and N-O-methyl attachment; seed 2 instead contains fluoromethyl groups, an N-rich bridged carbonyl core and a pendant cyclic dienol bearing an acyl fluoride. Optimizer median size is 27 heavy atoms, the same as Parent. Ring and aromatic content are abundant, but the particular N-F, acyl fluoride, hemiaminal/aminal-like environments and connected-ring geometry are far from a demonstrated routine synthesis.

The seed-2 acyl fluoride is an activated acyl environment; fluoromethyl, N-F and acyl-F groups cannot be treated as chemically interchangeable.
N-O attachments, cyclic dienol forms and aminal-like connected-ring environments remain unresolved by score or parse validity.

Explicit stereochemical/state identity and credible conformations of the partly saturated fused or bridged systems are missing where relevant.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child endpoints are 0.5900538040400954, 0.3957297846600013 and 0.5456103827984603 versus Parent 0.6942804632817005, 0.4999004646832901 and 0.6201223048692813. Fluorinated compact nitrogen/carbonyl arrangements associate with higher labels, whereas elemental fluorine scores 1.1043196211273875e-26 and an expanded linked dione assembly only 7.3198783640731225e-28. Within the late seed-2 family, replacing a fluoromethyl position by aldehyde accompanies a label of 0.02090290506987309 compared with the fluoromethyl leader's 0.5456103827984603; this is an observed local association, not proof of a general substituent effect. Parent also tolerates N-F and unusual small-ring connections. No conclusion that reactive fluorine attachment is chemically necessary or beneficial follows.

High-label structures retain direct nitrogen-halogen bonds, cyanate, cumulated ether unsaturation or acyl fluoride; other successful leaders have ordinary carbonyls and sulfur-free cyclic amines. The inherited n-93cd9a000278 neutral sulfur condition does not constrain all these local environments. This is not a new causal attribution or a transfer of historical numerical effects.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional alternatives that preserve relationships supported by accepted task-local feedback, while distinguishing complete functional-group environments rather than treating permitted sulfur or halogen presence as a plausibility certificate. Preserve useful sulfur-containing chemistry where supported; this evidence establishes neither the benefit of broader filtering nor which component creates a liability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap originating in n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, is re-observed in n-36a7bb9883ec under the same current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Leaders contain small connected closures, fused or bridged unsaturation and cumulated chains; some lowercase aromatic labels do not yield conventional aromatic-ring perception. Recognizable azaaryl amides and cyclic aryl amines are counterexamples to universal implausibility. Neither this report nor inherited sulfur membership supplies conformer or strain evidence.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to ring size, bridge connectivity and bond geometry, while retaining feasible aromatic, small-ring and medium-ring options supported by current feedback. Avoid inferring geometry from aromatic text or parse success. The association supplies no component-specific cause, chemical mediation or demonstrated endpoint benefit from such a change.

Every digest stereocentre-string and charged-string incidence is 0.0, yet leading cyclic amines and fluorinated connected-ring structures contain perceived unassigned centres. Neutral notation coexists with basic aliphatic amines; lack of written charge is not lack of ionizable chemistry. Achiral leading structures limit the gap's applicability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic arrangements remain unspecified, with protonation and tautomeric identity separately unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve configurational identity where chemically meaningful, treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately using legal task-local evidence. Do not infer a measured stereochemical penalty or component attribution from unspecified notation, and do not treat a generic added amine as the missing capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The context-preservation gap recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and retained through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180 recurs in n-36a7bb9883ec on the frozen Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Isolated small fragments commonly sit at score floors, while large linked heterocyclic assemblies can score far below compact complete arrangements. Distinct connected amine and carbonyl leaders also succeed, so the evidence does not support uniform shrinkage or universal size failure.

No fixed size threshold, blanket growth rule or extra aromatic mass preference follows. These output observations neither attribute fragmentation to a particular operator nor prove that size restrictions raise endpoints.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
